endorsements.quote: Under the GDPR, explicit consent will often be required, or will be the most appropriate lawful basis, for consultation recording in the use we propose; the precise lawful basis must nonetheless be determined under applicable national law and institutional arrangements, and consent to recording remains distinct both from consent to care and from the lawful basis for any subsequent processing ( 6 ).
Developers should accordingly report WER disaggregated by language and population rather than as a single aggregate figure.

Benefits should therefore be measured locally rather than assumed and, consistent with WHO guidance on AI for health, must not be allowed to accrue mainly to well-resourced, dominant-language settings ( 11 ).
Audits should be conducted by a body independent of line management, such as a quality-and-safety committee or a peer-review panel, rather than by an employer acting as both auditor and judge.

Specific safeguards are needed for minors, for patients with low literacy, and for multilingual encounters, where the information supporting consent must itself be intelligible; in emergencies, where valid consent is impracticable, recording should default to off.
It stressed, however, that the evidence remains heterogeneous and that clinician oversight of AI-generated notes is essential ( 16 ).

unlisted_practices: Adopt a minimum audit-ready transcript standard for ambient AI scribes, including timestamped speech turns, speaker diarization, audio deletion after a short disclosed verification window, pseudonymized transcript retention, and language- and population-disaggregated word error rate reporting, as a precondition for procurement.
Pilot the audit-ready transcript standard in parallel across high-income and low- and middle-income settings.
Retain consultation audio only for a short, access-controlled window before irreversible deletion.
Select audit cases by random sampling stratified by clinical risk, complemented by triggered review of predefined sentinel situations.
Apply explicit predefined audit criteria anchored to the guideline version in force on the consultation date, using a versioned, time-stamped reference corpus.
Engage a second independent reviewer with formal adjudication when audit reviewers disagree.
Give clinicians a documented right to review and contest audit findings before they are recorded, with a defined appeal mechanism.
Provide auditor training and periodic inter-rater reliability checks.
Firewall formative audit data from performance management and discipline, and state any crossing of that line explicitly in consent materials.
Validate the audit instrument before deployment and include an explicit indeterminate or insufficient-information outcome.
Interpret transcript-based audit findings alongside the relevant clinical record rather than in isolation.
Ensure consent to recording is genuinely free, with no consequence for declining, and reframe it around patient protection.
Clarify locally the medico-legal discoverability of transcripts before deployment.
Study effects of recording and auditing on clinician behavior and consultation authenticity as outcomes.
Prospectively validate transcript fidelity and audit conclusion validity against independent expert review before making the standard a binding procurement requirement.

Where full structural independence of audit is infeasible, ensure functional separation, transparent membership, declared conflicts of interest, multidisciplinary representation, documented procedures, and rights of review and appeal.
Benchmark audit software transcripts against contemporaneous guidelines and guarantee transparency, security, and reliability.

screen.reason: This is a perspective/policy commentary proposing recommendations and standards (such as a minimum audit-ready transcript standard and reframing consent) for governance and deployment of ambient AI in clinical care.
